items.q: Can a real appliance ever be 100% efficient?
items.correct: No — some energy is always wasted (usually as heat), so efficiency is always below 100%.
items.misconception: Yes, a 100%-efficient machine is achievable and common.
items.random_wrong: Efficiency measures how fast a device works.
items.why: Some energy is always dissipated to the surroundings. Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in, which is always less than 1 in practice.

items.q: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden one in the same room?
items.correct: Metal conducts thermal energy away from your hand faster, so it feels colder — both are at room temperature.
items.misconception: The metal spoon is actually at a lower temperature than the wooden one.
items.random_wrong: Metals contain 'cold' that flows into your hand.
items.why: In the same room both reach room temperature. Metal is a good conductor and draws heat from your warmer hand quickly, so it feels cold.

items.q: In which materials does convection transfer thermal energy?
items.correct: In fluids — liquids and gases — where particles are free to move and carry energy.
items.misconception: In solid metals, where convection currents carry the heat.
items.why: Convection needs particles free to move. In solids particles only vibrate in place, so solids transfer heat by conduction, not convection.
